offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

proposed.why: No tool calls are left, and the results so far point to provider failures that opened the circuit breaker.

findings.cause: From about 20:56, fake-provider began failing calls from payments-api on POST /v1/payments. Some calls got HTTP 500s, at a peak of about 0.36 to 0.48 per second, and others hung until payments-api's 3 s client read timeout (httpx.ReadTimeout at about 3006 ms). The timed-out calls are what push the p95 of POST /payments to about 3 s or more. These failures tripped payments-api's provider circuit breaker (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on). Since about 20:56:30 the open breaker rejects calls to /v1/payments without sending them. payments-api then leaves each payment pending and answers 503. The 503 rate rises from about 0.15/s to about 10/s while 201s fall to 0, which matches the alert's 96% 5xx. The root of the alert is the provider's errors and timeouts. The breaker turns them into fast 503s for almost every request.

evidence.shows: On payments-api, 503s jump from 0.15/s at 20:56:25 to 4.8/s at 20:56:55 and 10.0/s at 20:57:25. Over the same time 201s fall from 3.7/s to 0, which confirms the alert's symptom.

Every recent ERROR reads 'provider unavailable; payment left pending' with the error '/v1/payments not sent: the circuit breaker is open'. Some payment_ids, such as pmt_000397, pmt_000396 and pmt_000395, appear twice, which means clients are retrying.
Provider answers include HTTP 500s that rise from 20:56:05, at a peak of about 0.36 to 0.48/s against about 3/s of 200s. Provider calls then drop to 0 by 20:57:35 as the breaker stops sending them.
The p95 of provider calls that got an answer stays in milliseconds, so the slow requests are calls that never got an answer and that this histogram likely does not record.
Slow POST /payments traces cluster at about 3005 to 3012 ms, one per 10 to 13 s, which looks like the breaker's trial calls timing out. One trace took 6224 ms.

In a 3010 ms POST /payments that ended in 503, 3006 ms is spent in POST http://fake-provider:8000/v1/payments, which ends in httpx.ReadTimeout. The Redis and PostgreSQL spans take under 1 ms, which rules out the DB and Redis.

All containers were created together at 20:55:01–02, a fresh start, and no setting changed just before the failures. payments-api runs PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents and REFUND_CONNECTION=returned.

findings.left_open: The results do not show why the provider began timing out and answering 500s, since it is an outside party and sends no logs. I did not count ReadTimeouts directly: the client metric in c4 has no timeout series, so the timeout share is inferred from the traces. The breaker's thresholds, and whether it opens too eagerly on about 12% 500s plus timeouts, are unknown. Payments rejected while the breaker is open are left pending, and payments that timed out may have been charged at the provider without our knowing. I did not run the money check, so I cannot tell whether those are now out of step with the provider. The rise in 200s after 20:56:55 (c1) is unexplained; it may be idempotent replays of retried requests. The 6.2 s trace was not examined.

diagnosis.hypothesis: From about 20:56, fake-provider (outside our control) began answering about 11-14% of payments-api's POST /v1/payments with 500 and letting some calls hang until our 3 s read timeout. That tripped payments-api's circuit breaker (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on) between 20:56:25 and 20:56:55. While open, the breaker rejects calls without sending them, leaves each payment pending and answers 503 at about 10/s, while 201s fall to 0. Each half-open trial call, about every 10-13 s, again hangs for 3 s and times out, so the breaker stays open. This gives the 5xx share. The slow requests behind the p95 are the provider timeouts, from the onset and from the trials. The cause is the provider; the breaker works as designed and turns provider trouble into fast 503s. Left open: why the provider fails; the breaker's thresholds; and why some requests exceed one timeout (the 6.2 s trace, and the 3.7 s p95 above the 3 s timeout).

evidence.shows: payments-api 503s rise from 0.15/s at 20:56:25 to 4.82/s at 20:56:55 and 10.02/s at 20:57:25. 201s fall from 3.72/s to 0. 200s appear from 20:56:55, which is unexplained and possibly idempotent replays.

Every recent ERROR reads 'provider unavailable; payment left pending' with '/v1/payments not sent: the circuit breaker is open (the next trial call in N s)'. Some payment_ids repeat (pmt_000397, 000396, 000395, 000394), so clients are retrying into the open breaker.

Provider client calls: 500s at 0.36/s (20:56:05) and 0.48/s (20:56:35) against about 3/s of 200s, then both fall to 0 by 20:57:35 as the breaker stops sending. No ReadTimeout series appears, so this metric does not record the timeouts.
The p95 of provider calls that got an answer stays at 5-8 ms, so the slow requests are the unanswered (timed-out) calls, which this histogram does not record.

Slow POST /payments traces of 3005-3012 ms at 20:56:38, 20:56:48, 20:57:02 and 20:57:15, about 10-13 s apart, consistent with breaker trial calls timing out. One 6224 ms trace at 20:56:35 was not examined. The result is truncated (more_may_exist).

pmt_000363 at 20:57:15: 3010 ms, ended in 503. 3006 ms is in POST http://fake-provider:8000/v1/payments, which ended in httpx.ReadTimeout. The Redis and Postgres spans take under 1 ms, which rules them out.

All containers were created at 20:55:01-02 (a fresh start). No deploy or settings change came between the start and the failures at about 20:56, so no deploy is implicated. payments-api runs PROVIDER_BREAKER=on.

klaxon_provider_attempts_total has no outcome label (a single unlabelled series), so it gives no breakdown by outcome. It still shows 1.04/s at 20:57:31 while c4 shows 0 sent calls, a mismatch left unexplained.

proposed_fix.summary: There is no change to make on our side: the fault is the provider's. Keep the breaker on; turning it off would send every request into 3 s timeouts and more possible unknown charges. Watch for trial calls to succeed and the breaker to close. Afterwards, run the money check, and reconcile payments left pending and calls that timed out against the provider's records and webhooks. A timed-out call may have charged at the provider; payment-confirmer should mark those succeeded when their webhooks arrive.

diagnosis.blast_radius: No change is made. Payments keep failing with 503 and stay pending until the provider recovers. Calls that timed out may have charged at the provider without our knowing until their webhooks or the money check reveal them.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Nothing to undo, since no change is made. If the provider recovers but the breaker does not close, escalate to a human to inspect the breaker's settings.
